local_air_preassault.mix: small land-attack/recon element plus very small float-recon/water-air element
local_air_preassault.no_spawn: No fighter/Raiden detachment is created without a traceable allocation.

sensor_C2.local_radar: No confirmed operational local radar shipment; centerline warning relies on visual lookouts, radio/DF reports and aircraft/water-air reconnaissance.
sensor_C2.communications: Branch-standardized radio/telephone discipline, backup power where physically supplied, runners and local command cells are better maintained than historical-equivalent but remain vulnerable to bombardment.
sensor_C2.external_warning: Truk/Ponape/submarine/outer-island reports can raise strategic alert before local visual contact.

short_warning_fortification_11_20Feb: redisperse ammunition, water and medical stores
move selected command posts and crew shelters away from obvious beach/airfield targets
re-register mortar/artillery fires and anti-LVT/anti-armor lanes
hide tanks as local mobile reserves rather than expose them at the waterline
improve local reserve instructions and fallback routes
Eniwetok.hard_limit: Flat coral geography and 6-10 days of effective lesson-implementation time cannot create Palau/Saipan-style cave or deep reverse-slope fortress systems.
Eniwetok.reinforcement_reason: After Kwajalein falls, eastbound loaded transports face poor expected value. Surviving mobile personnel/shipping are preserved toward Ponape/Palau/western reserve rather than fed into an atoll likely to be assaulted next.

Truk.warning_system: A-grade integrated radar + visual posts + RI/DF + weather + plot + staged fighter/AA readiness with backup-power and field-service discipline.
Truk.precision_AA_fire_direction: 2 effective precision tracking/fire-direction channels centered; 1-3 serviceable band.
Truk.RWR_ESM: Selected metric-band passive warning/emitter-library capability supports cueing and search-sector narrowing, not range/identity and not centimetric-radar awareness.

warning_timeline.10_14Feb: Truk raid judged likely within roughly one-to-two weeks; high-value evacuation continues.
warning_timeline.15_16Feb: US fast-carrier sortie/replenishment signature raises major-operation confidence; search sectors shift east/northeast.
warning_timeline.17_19Feb: submarine/traffic/DF/ESM cues make Truk primary/co-primary target highly probable; sustained high alert, no stand-down after a negative search.
warning_timeline.19_20Feb: next-dawn attack becomes center estimate, but exact carrier track remains too poor for a large preemptive strike.

mobile_evacuation.Shokaku_Zuikaku_Soryu: Already continuing westward regeneration/preservation after the 2-Feb carrier battle; not returned to Truk defense.
mobile_evacuation.Hiryu: Propulsion-capable; emergency Truk deck/air-group repair and ferry/recovery-safe work, then westward evacuation centered about 13-16 Feb rather than waiting for full combat restoration.
mobile_evacuation.Akashi_and_mobile_repair: Remain only as long as needed for priority emergency work, then evacuate before centered HAILSTONE window.
mobile_evacuation.fleet_oilers_tenders_high_value_shipping: priority withdrawal 10-18 Feb; most high-speed/high-value mobile assets are not centered in lagoon at HAILSTONE dawn.

Truk.carrier_counter_sortie: NO-GO centered. Four Japanese hulls survive strategically, but Feb-2 carrier-air cadre losses and lack of fresh positive-EV TF58 geometry make a return toward Truk/Eniwetok irrational.
Truk.HAILSTONE_consequence: First US sweep faces a prepared capacity-limited defense rather than historical strategic surprise; lagoon target density is lower because evacuation has occurred.
